question: Why would a Canadian immigration museum combine accounts of exclusion with stories of newcomers' contributions instead of telling only a success story?
generated_answer: Maybe it's because we have this idea that we've got to be truthful and tell the whole story, and the whole story is not just the good things that happened. You know, it was very difficult to get into Canada in the early 20th century, even if you were white. And it was impossible for people of colour, for example, for African Americans, for Asian people. So, we've got to tell the whole story, and that means the story of exclusion. But I think it also means that, on the other side, we have to tell the story of success, of overcoming, of contribution. And one of the things that we really want to do at the museum is to help people understand that Canada is a better place because of the contribution of newcomers. We're not just taking people in. We're enriching ourselves through the contributions of newcomers. That's the whole story, and we think it's a better way of doing things. Telling the whole story means telling both the good and the bad. It means telling the story of exclusion and the story of success. It means helping people understand that Canada is a better place because of the contribution of newcomers. It's not just a matter of taking people in. We're enriching ourselves through the contributions of newcomers.
